title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM `Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id)` and `AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id)`, which employ parameterised queries. No raw SQL or string interpolation is present.

The endpoint fetches a Rule or AlertRule by the user‑controlled `rule_id` from the URL without verifying that the rule belongs to the project (or organization) implied by the request path. This can allow an attacker to mute/modify snooze state of rules they should not have access to (IDOR).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a check that the fetched rule belongs to the `project` (e.g., `if rule.project_id != project.id: raise PermissionDenied`). Also ensure the rule's organization matches `project.organization`. Consider using existing permission helpers that validate object ownership before allowing snooze creation.
